notes.text: The second course of St. Paul xvi-xix
His third, as far as Rom. xix-xxviii THE ACTS
But ye shall receive power — and shall be witnesses to me - That is, ye shall be empowered to witness my Gospel, both by your preaching and suffering.
A Sabbath-day's journey — The Jews generally fix this to two thousand cubits, which is not a mile.

They went up into the upper room — The upper rooms, so frequently mentioned in Scripture, were chambers in the highest part of the house, set apart by the Jews for private prayer. These, on account of their being so retired and convenient, the apostles now used for all the offices of religion. Matt. x, 2; Mark iii, 14; Luke vi, 13.
His brethren -- his near kinsmen, who for some time did not believe; it seems not till near his death.

glossa.text: *It is not for you to know.* He does not say, it will not be, but *it is not:* noting that they are still weak, and therefore not fit for the knowing of the secret: but when he says: *It is not for you to know,* he shows that he himself knows, whose are all things that are the Father's, but that it is not expedient for them to know, but that they should so live as though they were to be judged daily. *Which the Father.* The time of that kingdom, he says, is so secret that it lies open only to the knowledge of the Father, *but you shall receive the power of the Holy Spirit,* that what through the weakness of the flesh you cannot do, you may be able to do out of the power of the Holy Spirit. *In his own power.* This he said excusably as true man, but there is only one power of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit: the Son also is the power of the Father.

*But you shall receive.* The knowledge of the times is taken away, but the divine help of which they stand in need is applied: in this manner, when something is taken from children, another thing is given lest they be utterly saddened. *Of the Holy Spirit coming upon you.* When the Spirit shall come upon you, he will not bring the kingdom of Israel, or the kingdom of God in Israel, as you think, but he will bestow upon you the power of bearing witness of me, and the time of that kingdom is so far off, that first the fame of the Gospel shall run through not only Jerusalem, but all the borders of Judaea and of Samaria, and even the bounds of the world round about. *In Jerusalem and in all Judaea.* The consequence of order is preserved in the names of the places: to Jerusalem succeeds the nearest province of Judaea, to which Samaria is joined by situation, and thereafter the fellowship of the whole earth is brought in. *In Jerusalem.* Mystically: in the vision of peace, in the confession of the true faith: in the keeping of the commandments of God: and he foretold that they would preach among those who shall have made themselves strangers from the earth, through whom, as through the spokes of a wheel, from the middle of the earth where he wrought salvation, spiritual grace and saving doctrine flowed out through the whole world.

*And when he had said these things.* Mark records it otherwise, saying: *And the Lord Jesus indeed, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven ((Matth. XXVIII))*. But because Luke added more significantly: *When he had said these things, he was lifted up,* he shows that, those discourses being finished which he had recorded, the Lord ascended the heavens.

*Galilaeans, why stand you looking up to heaven?* In whom there ought to be a more prudent understanding, because the Galilaeans excelled the rest of the Jews in wisdom. Or, Galilaeans, the changeable, because by the instability of their sense they will have forgotten the commandments of God.

*Then they returned,* etc. The return of the apostles from Mount Olivet to Jerusalem signifies the Church, which, ascending from the active into the contemplative, descends again into the active manner of life. For Mount Olivet was called by the ancients the mount of three lights: namely of the lamp shining out from the temple, and of the sun rising on the other side, and of the oil, a natural light on the mount itself: which three things befit perfection, on account of the light of the divine Word shining out from the Church, on account of the brightness of the sun of justice, on account of the lustre of a pure conscience.

*And when they were come in.* In the Greek it is put thus: *When they had entered the city, they went up into the upper room, where were abiding Peter,* etc. In the Greek the order of the names is thus: *Peter and Andrew, James and John, Simon Zelotes and Judas of James. The upper room,* etc. ((BEDA.)) It is a place in the upper part, signifying that they who are lifted from the earth ascend to the higher things of knowledge and of virtue.

The upper room is called the third roof, a figure of charity built up upon faith and hope. But charity is poured forth in our hearts through the Spirit. *Peter and John.* Peter is put first, because he is prince and shepherd. Peter and John are deservedly put first, who ran together to the tomb, because they loved more than the rest. The first (if it is right to say it) loved more than the rest: the other, Jesus loved most. The catalogue of the apostles is therefore set down, lest outside these any false ones be received: and equal places of each are set down, the degrees of merits distinguishing them.

These are the twelve sons of Jacob; the twelve fountains of the desert, which Israel found in Elim; the twelve loaves of proposition; the twelve stones on the vestment of the high priest; the twelve signs of the zodiac; the twelve stones of the altar; the twelve stones lifted out of the Jordan; the twelve oxen under the brazen sea; the twelve stars in the crown of the spouse; the twelve foundations; the twelve gates; the twelve months of the year; the twelve hours of the day; the twelve fruits of the tree of life.

*Zelotes. ((BEDA.))* Zelotes is the same who in the Gospels is called Chananaeus. Chana is interpreted *zeal.* For he was of a village of Galilee where the Lord turned water into wine. He, after James his brother, ruled the Church of Jerusalem.

The son of perdition perishing, the number of the apostles remained imperfect, for according to the likeness of the moon the Church waxes and wanes: but old things pass away, and new things are made.

*Mary,* etc. The Virgin is distinguished from the women, who nevertheless is sometimes called woman not for corruption, but for sex. Behold, the beginning of the nascent Church is adorned with the flower of virginity. *In the midst of the brethren.* That is, of the sons, whose Father in heaven is one.

Peter is said to have stood in the midst: as it were condescending with a common compassion. This example is to be taken by the shepherds of the Church.

This number of a hundred and twenty agrees with the age of Moses, that as under this number, Moses being dead, Jesus succeeded, who led the people into the land of promise, so to the old law the princedom of Christ succeeded in the Church, leading the true Israel to the kingdom of heaven.

notes.text: Jah — Is an abbreviation of the name Jehovah, which the Heathens pronounced Jao. Before him - Before the ark where he is present, as David is said to dance before the Lord, upon this occasion, 2 Sam. vi, 14.
Habitation — In heaven.
Rebellious — Those who rebel against God.
Wentest — In the cloudy pillar, as their captain leading them up out of Egypt.
Dropped — Poured down great showers, which accompanied those mighty thunders.
Weary — Dry and thirsty, and parched with excessive heat, and ready to faint for want of rain, chap. lxiii, 1.

Thy congregation — The people of Israel. It - This land for the use of thy people: which God did by designing it for them, and expelling the old inhabitants; by furnishing it with all sorts of provisions, and making it fruitful by his special blessing. Poor - Such thy really were, when God undertook the conduct of them into Canaan.

glossa.text: *Let God arise, and let them be scattered. ((Ibid.))* He confidently wishes for what he knows will be. *And let them that hate him flee.* ((HIER.)) Or it can be read of the penitent, etc., *as far as* that, when the fire of the Holy Spirit is applied by the tears of penitence, their hardness may be dissolved. *That hate him.* ((AUG.)) Let the obstinate be taken away from the presence of him who is everywhere present; a grave curse, that they should will and strive after what can in no wise come to pass.

*As smoke faileth.* ((CAS.)) Smoke from a flame vanishes in its rising; so sinners bring forth smoky deeds out of the flame of wickedness, and by that very lifting up they fail. *As it melteth.* ((AUG.)) It can be said of the penitent; or, in the judgment the wicked will be taken away from the face of God: who will be a fire for the punishment of the ungodly, and a light for the just.

*Let them feast.* ((CASS., AUG.)) In the delights which are in the sight of God. *And let them be delighted,* this can delight them, that they are glad *qui* because their gladness is not to be ended.

*Sing ye to God.* ((AUG.)) He turns himself to those to whom he has given so great a hope, and exhorts them. *Who ascendeth.* The new life will not receive him unless the old has died; or, by rising again he overcame the fall of the body. *Upon the going down.* ((CAS.)) The going down of death befalls him upon whom the sun of justice rises. And lest thou doubt who this may be, because *the Lord is his name,* a name essential to him, whom the Jews slew as a common man. *In the sight.* The consideration of the reward to come mitigates hardships.

*Of orphans.* ((AUG.)) Whose father, the world and the devil, is dead, and their mother, concupiscence. *Widows,* for whom their husband, error, dies; in whom God dwells, whom he gathers, whom he draws, because out of widows and orphans he makes himself a temple, in which he is.

*God who maketh to dwell.* ((HIER.)) In the Hebrew it stands: *But the Lord maketh monks to dwell in a house,* in whom sin does not dwell together. *Of one manner.* ((AUG.)) Of one mind, thinking one thing, etc., *as far as* not by merits, whence he adds: *Who bringeth out them that were bound. He bringeth out them that were bound.* ((CAS.)) Out of hell, the devil being bound. *Who provoke.* Blasphemers against God. Or, by persecuting, buried in tombs, in stinking carnal things, so that they neither will nor can walk. *They provoke.* ((AUG.)) By resisting justice, since they are altogether dead in dead works; but the bound do will to walk, and cannot; these are loosed by grace, those are raised up.

*O God, when thou didst go forth.* ((CAS.)) A Diapsalmus concerning the word of the Gospel, by the going forth of Christ. *O God, when thou didst go forth.* Truly thou bringest out, because his going forth was prefigured before Israel, when he appeared in the pillar of cloud and of fire in the desert, and filled them with manna. ((AUG.)) *A going forth,* when he appeared to men through his humanity, or when *he bringeth out them that were bound,* that is, raises them up. *He passed into the desert,* when he came to the Gentiles. ((BASIL.)) *Thou didst go forth.* As if he should say: when thou wast about to pass over that solitude which had not yet received the splendour of light, the earth indeed thou didst shake and stir *commovistis*; read *commovisti*, 2nd sg., but from heaven thou didst distil the drops of thy grace.

*The earth was moved.* Because then earthly men were moved at seeing such great wonders. *The heavens dropped down at the face of God:* manna, when in the manner of a dripping manna came down from the face of God, whose presence was known by the pillar. ((AUG.)) Mount Sinai smoked at the face of God (according to another reading) when Moses received the law there.

*A rain.* This is what the heavens dropped down, manna, *a voluntary rain* which would satisfy the will of that nation, greedy to eat. *Thou shalt set apart, O God, for thine inheritance.* Because he did not give to other nations what he then gave to the Jews. *It was weakened,* etc. For a time, while it did not believe in Christ. ((CAS.)) *He hath made it perfect.* God made his inheritance perfect, when he admitted the Gentiles to fill it up. He adds whereby he made it perfect.

*Living creatures.* That is, thy nations, when they believe, dwell in the inheritance, that is, in the Church. He sets forth what the living creatures are. *Thou hast prepared:* he means the predestined, because from the origin of the world they were made ready. ((AUG.)) Or, *mount at the face of the God of Israel,* supply "dropped down", etc., *as far as* in whom grace superabounded. ((CAS.)) These things mystically, but according to the figure, etc., *as far as* he sends therefore to the mystery. ((AUG.)) Certain books do not have *mount,* but *at the face of the God of Sinai, of Israel;* that is, he who gave the law to the people of Israel: because he who gave the law through Moses, whereby he might terrify, gave also the blessing through the Apostles, whereby he might set free. *In sweetness* ((CAS.)) *Sweetness* is that whereby good is done, not from fear of punishment, but from delight in justice.

notes.text: Wonder not at the burning which is among you — This is the literal meaning of the expression. It seems to include both martyrdom itself, which so frequently was by fire, and all the other sufferings joined with, or previous to, it; which is permitted by the wisdom of God for your trial. Be not surprised at this.

But as ye partake of the sufferings of Christ — chap. 1, while ye suffer for his sake, rejoice in hope of more abundant glory. For the measure of glory answers the measure of suffering; and much more abundantly.

If ye are reproached for Christ — Reproaches and cruel mockings were always one part of their sufferings. The Spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you - The same Spirit which was upon Christ, Luke iv, 18. He is here termed, the Spirit of glory, conquering all reproach and shame, and the Spirit of God, whose Son, Jesus Christ is. On their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified - That is, while they are blaspheming Christ, you glorify him in the midst of your sufferings, chap. 16.

glossa.text:
*Dearly beloved, be ye not as strangers.* If you suffer the heat of tribulations which are brought against reason for your trial and glory, do not for that reason think yourselves to be exiles from the members of Christ, and do not wonder at the evils brought upon you, that through them God may tempt and prove you, because it is an ancient and frequent thing that the elect of God, for eternal salvation, suffer adversities in the present.

VERS 14.-- *You shall be blessed,* etc. He who suffers for the name of Christ is blessed; for you ought not to believe that you suffer without reward, as those do who suffer for their own crimes, and are punished against their will.

*His Spirit resteth upon you.* Because they shall rest upon you that suffer, both in the present in part unto working well, and in the future perfectly unto rewarding.

notes.text: For himself, ver. 1-5. John xvii, 1-5
For the apostles, ver. 6-19; John xvii, 6-19 and again, ver. 24- 26. John xvii, 24-26
For all believers, ver. 20-23. John xvii, 20-23 And

For the world, ver. 21-23. John xvii, 21-23 In his prayer he comprises all he had said from 31, and seals, as it were, all he had hitherto done, beholding things past, present, and to come. This chapter contains the easiest words, and the deepest sense of any in all the Scripture: yet is here no incoherent rhapsody, but the whole is closely and exactly connected.

1. Father - This simplicity of appellation highly became the only- begotten Son of God; to which a believer then makes the nearest approach, when he is fullest of love and humble confidence. The hour is come - The appointed time for it; glorify thy Son - The Son glorified the Father, both before and after his own glorification. When he speaks to the Father he does not style himself the Son of man.

2. As thou hast given him power over all flesh - This answers to glorify thy Son. That he may give eternal life, &c.-This answers to that thy Son may glorify thee. To all whom thou hast given him - To all believers. This is a clear proof that Christ designed his sacrifice should avail for all: yea, that all flesh, every man, should partake of everlasting life. For as the Father had given him power over all flesh, so he gave himself a ransom for all.

3. To know - By loving, holy faith, thee the only true God - The only cause and end of all things; not excluding the Son and the Holy Ghost, no more than the Father is excluded from being Lord, 1 Cor. viii, 6; but the false gods of the heathens; and Jesus Christ - As their prophet, priest, and king: this is life eternal - It is both the way to, and the essence of, everlasting happiness.

4. I have finished the work - Thus have I glorified thee, laying the foundation of thy kingdom on earth.
The glory which I had — He does not say received - He always had it, till he emptied himself of it in the days of his flesh.

I have manifested thy name — All thy attributes; and in particular thy paternal relation to believers; to the men whom thou hast given me - The apostles, and so ver. 12. They were thine - By creation, and by descent from Abraham. And thou hast given them me - By giving them faith in what I have spoken. So ver. 9.
Now they know that all things — Which I have done and spoken, are of thee - And consequently right and true.
They have received them — By faith.

I pray not for the world — Not in these petitions, which are adapted to the state of believers only. (He prays for the world at ver. 21, 23, that they may believe - That they may know God hath sent him.) This no more proves that our Lord did not pray for the world, both before and afterward, than his praying for the apostles alone, ver. 6-19, proves that he did not pray for them also which shall believe through their word, ver. 20.

All things that are mine are thine, and that are thine are mine — These are very high and strong expressions, too grand for any mere creature to use; as implying that all things whatsoever, inclusive of the Divine nature, perfections, and operations, are the common property of the Father and the Son. And this is the original ground of that peculiar property, which both the Father and the Son have in the persons who were given to Christ as Mediator; according to what is said in the close of the verse, of his being glorified by them; namely, believing in him, and so acknowledging his glory.
Keep them through thy name — Thy power, mercy, wisdom, that they may be one - with us and with each other; one body, separate from the world: as we are - By resemblance to us, though not equality.

glossa.text: *These things spoke.* Not only the things [said] at the supper, but also those from the beginning. But chiefly he says that the things at the supper were said for this cause, that in him they might have peace. This is the peace for which we are Christians, for which we are steeped in the sacraments, for which we are instructed in every way, for which we have received the Spirit as a pledge, for which we believe in him and hope, and are kindled with love of him. This is consolation in afflictions and deliverance. *Father, the hour is come.* He could have prayed in silence, but in praying he is also a teacher, and makes his prayer known, which is the edification both of those present and of those to come. *The hour is come.* Not with fate urging, but with God disposing, who without time ordained all the things that come to pass through times in a fitting order. *Glorify thy Son.* Humility began in the passion, glory in the resurrection. The hour of the passion is come, the hour of sowing humility; do not defer the glory of the resurrection, *that thy Son may glorify thee.* And thus the glory of the Father can neither be increased nor diminished in itself. Among men it was less while he was known in Judaea alone, but through the resurrection of the Son he became known everywhere. *That thy Son may glorify thee.* In the knowledge of men, as thou hast given, as far as *that they may know thee, and him whom thou hast sent.* For the Father cannot be glorified in the knowledge of man unless he be known through whom he is glorified, that is, unless the people become known; and this is the glorification of the Father, which is not about the apostles alone but also about all believers.

*And this is,* etc. The order [is], *That they may know thee, and him whom thou hast sent,* that is, Christ with the Spirit, who is of both, to be the one and only true God. If therefore the Son glorifies thee in that manner in which thou hast given him power over every creature, and hast so given it, *that all that thou hast given him, he may give them life everlasting:* And *this is life everlasting, that they may know thee.* So therefore does the Son glorify thee, that he may make thee known to all whom thou hast given him. *That they may know thee.* What is here from the Father, in the world to come will be fully. He therefore who advances in knowledge tends the more to live. But when knowledge shall be full, there will be praise without end. And this is that glorification; but first he is glorified here, while he becomes known to the faithful; whence: *I have glorified thee upon earth.*

*I have finished the work.* That is, as if he said openly of what is to come, I will glorify [thee], by preaching to the Gentiles. I will finish the work, because it is already done by predestination; and what most certainly is to be is to be held as already done. This predestination he opens more manifestly in his own glorification, saying: *Which I had with thee before the world was;* that is, as I then had it with thee in predestination before the times, so now in reality make it in the world in time. *Thou hast given me,* etc. Wherein grace is noted. For he has nothing in the man which he has not received.

*To men.* All these things can be said of all the faithful who are to be. And this is that glorification by which the Son, being glorified, glorifies the Father upon earth, according to which the past stands for the future.
*They were thine. ((AUG.))* These were the Father's, as all things are, etc., *as far as* because he was not yet man.

*They have known.* Lest the knowledge should be thought already made through sight, he adds: They have believed truly; not in that manner in which it was when he said, Now you believe, the hour cometh that you be scattered. But not even yet were they such; rather he foretells what they will be when the Spirit has been received, without whom they did not even keep the word which he had spoken.

*I pray for them.* The first prayer was: *Glorify the Son, that the Son may glorify thee,* and he pursued these things and concluded in the faith of believers. Now he prays for them, that the Father may keep those whom he himself has left in body.

*And all mine.* For the Father did not lose because he gave to the Son, since the Son further adds: *All mine thine and thine mine are.* Of the only-begotten Son are all the things that are the Father's, through this, that he himself is also God, and, being also born of the Father, is equal to the Father.

*Keep them.* That they may be one in their own nature, as we also in ours are one; and therefore he does not say, that they may be one with us, or that we and they may be one as we are one, because they are not of the same nature with God, as the Son, according to that which he is God, is one with the Father.

hymns.title: Source and Sovereign, Rock and Cloud
And God will raise you up on eagle's wings
Glorious things of thee are spoken
We shall tell among the peoples
Filled with the Spirit's power, with one accord
See how great a flame aspires

echoes.text: yes, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
echoes.note: 'You will be witnesses... to the uttermost parts of the earth' closely tracks the Servant's commission to be 'a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.' Volume: the phrase 'to the end(s) of the earth' is a distinctive LXX echo (heos eschatou tes ges). Recurrence: strong — Luke cites Isa 49:6 explicitly at Acts 13:47 and alludes again, making it a structural thesis statement for the book. Thematic coherence: very high; this verse programs Acts' whole geographic movement. A leading candidate in the history of interpretation for the key to Acts.

echoes.text: “You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh, “With my servant whom I have chosen; that you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he. Before me there was no God formed, neither will there be after me. I myself am Yahweh; and besides me there is no savior. I have declared, I have saved, and I have shown; and there was no strange god among you. Therefore you are my witnesses”, says Yahweh, “and I am God.
echoes.note: 'You will be witnesses to me' echoes the Lord's words to Israel, 'You are my witnesses... and my servant whom I have chosen.' Volume: the witness-language is distinctive and combined with election (the apostles 'whom he had chosen,' v.2). Recurrence: the witness motif saturates Acts. Thematic coherence: high; Israel's vocation to testify to the one God is transferred to the apostles. Overlaps with Isa 49:6 in the same Isaianic Servant matrix.

echoes.text: He changes the times and the seasons; he removes kings, and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding;
echoes.note: 'It isn't for you to know times or seasons (chronous e kairous) which the Father has set within his own authority' echoes Daniel's 'he changes times and seasons (kairous kai chronous)... he reveals deep and hidden things.' Volume: the paired words 'times and seasons' are a distinctive doublet shared with LXX Daniel. Thematic coherence: high; both texts locate the calendar of the kingdom in God's sovereign reserve. Recurrence: 'times and seasons' as a fixed pair recurs in Jewish apocalyptic. Solid mid-level link.

echoes.text: In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen, and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old; that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and all the nations who are called by my name,” says Yahweh who does this.
echoes.note: The apostles' question, 'are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?', sits atop the prophetic hope of the rebuilt 'booth of David' that the remnant and the nations might seek the Lord. Volume: no shared wording here. Recurrence: notable — Luke quotes Amos 9:11-12 at the Jerusalem council (Acts 15:16-17) precisely to interpret how the restored Davidic kingdom includes the nations, which is exactly the tension between v.6 (Israel) and v.8 (the earth). Thematic coherence good; low confidence because the link is conceptual and back-referenced rather than verbal here.
echoes.lxxText: In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and will rebuild the ruins of it, and will set up the parts thereof that have been broken down, and will build it up as in the ancient days: that the remnant of men, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name is called, may earnestly seek me, saith the Lord who does all these things.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: 'A cloud received him out of their sight,' and the angels promise he 'will come back in the same way.' Volume: the cloud as the vehicle of the exalted Son of Man is the distinctive Danielic image (one 'coming with the clouds of heaven'). Luke reverses and reaffirms the trajectory — ascent now, return on clouds later. Recurrence: strong in Luke-Acts' Son-of-Man Christology (Luke 21:27; 22:69). Thematic coherence high; the cloud signals heavenly enthronement, the very kingship the disciples asked about in v.6.

echoes.text: As they still went on, and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
echoes.note: Jesus 'was taken up' while the apostles 'looked steadfastly into the sky,' patterned on Elijah taken up to heaven as Elisha watched ('if you see me as I am taken from you...'). Volume: shared motif of a witnessed bodily assumption, the gaze of the successor(s), and the transfer of spirit/Spirit immediately afterward (Elisha's double portion ~ the apostles' Spirit-baptism). Recurrence: Luke deliberately uses Elijah-Elisha typology throughout (e.g., Luke 9:51, 9:61-62). Thematic coherence very high; the disciples' Spirit-empowerment in v.8 mirrors Elisha's inheritance. A staple of the history of interpretation.

echoes.text: His feet will stand in that day on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split in two, from east to west, making a very great valley. Half of the mountain will move toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
echoes.note: The ascension and promised return occur at/over the Mount of Olives (named in v.12), the very mountain on which 'the feet of the Lord' will stand on the eschatological day of his coming. Volume: low verbal overlap, but the geography is pointed and the angels' 'will come back in the same way' resonates with Zechariah's theophanic return to that mountain. Thematic coherence strong; recurrence modest. The setting makes this more than coincidental, hence echo/medium.

echoes.text: Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.
echoes.note: Jesus' bodily removal to heaven faintly recalls Enoch, who 'walked with God, and he was not, for God took him' (LXX: 'God translated him'). Volume: low; only the shared motif of a righteous one taken without ordinary death. Recurrence: Enoch/assumption traditions were live in Second Temple Judaism. Coherence modest. Included as a faint, contested member of the 'assumption of the righteous' background alongside Elijah.

echoes.text: You shall measure outside of the city for the east side two thousand cubits, and for the south side two thousand cubits, and for the west side two thousand cubits, and for the north side two thousand cubits, the city being in the middle. This shall be the suburbs of their cities.
echoes.note: The distance from Olivet is 'a Sabbath day's journey,' a halakhic measure derived from the limits set around the Levitical cities and the camp (cf. the 2,000-cubit reckoning) and the Sabbath-rest command. Volume: the phrase reflects later legal interpretation rather than a quotation, but its scriptural root is the camp/city boundary measures. Thematic coherence modest. Faint, halakhic background note.

echoes.text: His feet will stand in that day on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split in two, from east to west, making a very great valley. Half of the mountain will move toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
echoes.note: The explicit naming of 'the mountain called Olivet' reinforces the eschatological resonance of the Mount of Olives as the place of the Lord's coming (Zech 14:4). Volume low (toponym only). Recurrence: Olivet frames both ascension and the Lukan passion. Coherence ties back to the return promised in v.11. Listed at low confidence as a topographic echo.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

places.name: Judea
places.id: The Roman administrative province (later procuratorial province) covering the southern hill country of Israel — Jerusalem, the Judean wilderness, and territory south to the Negev. The Greco-Roman successor to the Hasmonean and Herodian Iudaea. Pin sits in the central hill country.

places.name: Samaria
places.id: The central hill-country region between Galilee (north) and Judea (south), centered on the city of Sebaste / Samaria (Sebastiya) — the old capital of Omri (1 Kgs 16:24) refounded by Herod. Distinct from the city: pin sits in the regional centre.

places.name: Galilee
places.id: The northern region of Roman-period Palestine, bounded by the Jezreel valley (south), the Lebanese mountains (north), the Mediterranean (west), and the Jordan / Sea of Galilee (east). Subdivided into Lower Galilee (the Jesus traditions are mostly here) and Upper Galilee.

places.name: Mount of Olives
places.id: The ridge east of Jerusalem rising c. 100 m above the city across the Kidron valley. Site of the Bethphage and Bethany approach (Mk 11), the Ascension tradition, and (2 Sam 15:30, Zech 14:4) earlier covenantal geography. Modern Jebel et-Tur preserves the name.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: kill utterly the old man, the young man and the virgin, and little children and women; but don’t come near any man on whom is the mark: and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the old men that were before the house.
echoes.note: "Judgment to begin with the household of God" (4:17) draws directly on the command to begin the slaughter "at my sanctuary," i.e., judgment commencing with God's own house before the wider world. Core source for the verse's logic.

echoes.text: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid in the earth; how much more the wicked and the sinner!
echoes.note: "If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner?" (4:18) cites Proverbs 11:31 in its LXX form verbatim (the LXX renders the Hebrew as a saved/scarcely-saved a fortiori). Formula-cited proverb.
echoes.lxxText: If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?

echoes.text: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
echoes.note: The "fiery trial... to test you" (4:12) draws on the wisdom/prophetic metaphor of the crucible refining metal as God tests his people; cf. the smelting imagery the verse shares with Proverbs 17:3.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap; and he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver; and they shall offer to Yahweh offerings in righteousness.
echoes.note: The refining fire that purifies (4:12) echoes the Lord's coming as a refiner's fire who purges the sons of Levi; this same Malachi context (judgment beginning at the temple) also feeds 4:17.

echoes.text: I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say, ‘It is my people;’ and they will say, ‘Yahweh is my God.’”
echoes.note: "I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and try them as gold" closely parallels the testing-by-fire of God's remnant in 4:12. Strong thematic and verbal coherence.

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: "The Spirit of glory and of God rests on you" (4:14) reworks "the Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him" (the messianic endowment), transferring the resting Spirit from the Messiah to the reproached believer. Verbal "rests/Spirit" link.

echoes.text: For, behold, I begin to work evil at the city which is called by my name; and should you be utterly unpunished? You shall not be unpunished; for I will call for a sword on all the inhabitants of the earth, says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: "I begin to bring evil on the city which is called by my name, and should you go utterly unpunished?" supplies the a fortiori structure of 4:17 (if it begins with us, what of the disobedient?). Strong conceptual parallel.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies. “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap; and he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and […]
echoes.note: The Lord suddenly coming to his temple to judge begins purifying judgment at the house of God (4:17), reinforcing Ezekiel 9; the same passage's refining fire underlies 4:12.

echoes.text: Into your hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, Yahweh, God of truth.
echoes.note: "Entrust their souls to him" (4:19) echoes "Into your hand I commit my spirit," the psalm of committing oneself to God amid suffering (also on Christ's lips, Luke 23:46). Verbal commit-to-God parallel.

echoes.text: For you, God, have tested us. You have refined us, as silver is refined.
echoes.note: "You, God, have tested us; you have refined us as silver is refined" supplies the same trial-as-refining figure behind 4:12. Faint, one of several refining texts.

echoes.text: Remember, Lord, the reproach of your servants, how I bear in my heart the taunts of all the mighty peoples, With which your enemies have mocked, Yahweh, with which they have mocked the footsteps of your anointed one.
echoes.note: Being "insulted for the name of Christ" (4:14) evokes the psalmist bearing the reproach of God's servants and of the LORD's anointed; shared reproach-for-the-name motif. Cf. Psalm 69:9.

echoes.text: “You only have I chosen of all the families of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all of your sins.”
echoes.note: "You only have I known... therefore I will punish you" expresses the same principle that election intensifies rather than exempts from judgment, undergirding 4:17. Thematic.

echoes.text: But now thus says Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
echoes.note: "A faithful Creator" (4:19) draws on the prophetic confession of God as the faithful Creator and Redeemer of his people who can be trusted in trial. Faint, supports the entrusting-to-Creator theme.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: 'You gave him authority over all flesh' (v2) reprises the one like a son of man to whom 'was given dominion... that all peoples should serve him.' High Volume in the verbal pairing of given-authority + universal scope; Recurrence is strong since Johannine and Synoptic Son of Man material draws steadily on Dan 7. Coherent with John's glorification-by-exaltation logic.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh, Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, don’t let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God' (v3) recasts 'let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me, that I am the LORD.' Knowing God as the supreme good is the load-bearing parallel; high Coherence with John's salvific epistemology and strong Recurrence of this Jeremianic theme in Second-Temple piety.

echoes.text: “Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed. When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born; while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world. When he established the heavens, I was […]
echoes.note: 'The glory which I had with you before the world existed' (v5) figures the Son after personified Wisdom, who was beside God 'before the beginning of the earth' rejoicing in the inhabited world. Availability and Recurrence are high in Johannine Logos/Wisdom Christology (cf. John 1); the conceptual fit (preexistent agent of creation, delight/glory shared) is strong though the wording is not quoted.

echoes.text: Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God.
echoes.note: 'Before the world existed' (v5) echoes 'before the mountains were brought forth, or ever you had formed the earth... from everlasting.' The temporal formula for divine pre-creation eternity coheres with the Son's claim to preexistent glory; Volume modest, supported by the same idiom in Wisdom traditions.

echoes.text: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
echoes.note: 'That they should know you' as life (v3) resonates with 'I desire... the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.' Knowledge of God as the heart of the covenant relationship supplies a coherent OT substratum, though John intensifies it to eternal life.

echoes.text: For to be acquainted with you is perfect righteousness, And to know your dominion is the root of immortality.
echoes.note: 'To know your power is the root of immortality' is a remarkably close conceptual antecedent to 'this is eternal life, that they should know you' (v3). Availability (deuterocanonical, pre-Johannine) and Coherence are high; the equation knowledge-of-God = immortality is nearly verbal, strengthening the case as a Second-Temple bridge.

echoes.text: Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one.
echoes.note: 'The only true God' (v3) presses the Shema's confession of the one LORD. Monotheistic exclusivity is the coherent backdrop, and John's 'only true' renders the Shema's uniqueness; modest Volume since the wording is interpretive rather than quoted.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: 'Before the world existed' (v5) presupposes the creation account's absolute beginning, the backdrop against which the Son's pre-cosmic glory is asserted. Faint by itself but coherent with John 1:1's deliberate 'In the beginning' recasting of Genesis.

echoes.text: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished. On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
echoes.note: 'I have accomplished the work which you gave me to do' (v4) faintly mirrors God finishing the work of creation and resting. Possible figural completion-of-work motif, but the language is generic; marked contested for low Volume.

echoes.text: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of Yahweh’s glory, as the waters cover the sea.
echoes.note: 'They should know you' coupled with 'glorify' (vv1-3) faintly recalls 'the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD.' Knowledge-plus-glory cluster offers thematic coherence but Volume is low and diffuse.

echoes.text: He created me from the beginning before the world; And to the end I will not fail.
echoes.note: Personified Wisdom 'created before the ages' supplies a Second-Temple analogue to the Son's glory 'before the world existed' (v5). Reinforces the Wisdom-preexistence channel alongside Proverbs 8; low independent Volume.

echoes.text: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’” God said moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the children of Israel this, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.
echoes.note: 'I revealed your name to the people' (v6) figures Jesus' mission as the disclosure of the divine Name first given at the bush, where God names himself I AM and 'this is my name forever.' John's recurrent egō eimi sayings make this Name-revelation channel highly coherent and recurrent.

echoes.text: He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.”
echoes.note: 'I revealed your name' (v6) draws on the LORD's promise 'I will proclaim before you my name, the LORD.' The pattern of God making his Name known through a mediator coheres with the prayer's theology; Volume modest but the Name-proclamation motif recurs across the chapter (vv11,26).

echoes.text: Yahweh descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed Yahweh’s name. Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth, keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the […]
echoes.note: The Sinai theophany where the LORD 'proclaimed the name of the LORD' (grace, truth, steadfast love) underlies 'I revealed your name' (v6) and feeds John's grace-and-truth framework. Coherent and recurrent with John 1:14-17; the manifest-Name act is the shared structure.

echoes.text: Therefore my people shall know my name. Therefore they shall know in that day that I am he who speaks; behold, it is I.”
echoes.note: 'Therefore my people shall know my name' anticipates 'I revealed your name to the people... they have known' (vv6-7). The eschatological Name-knowledge promised to the elect people coheres tightly with Jesus' report to the Father; moderate Volume via the shared name/know pairing.

echoes.text: I will declare your name to my brothers. In the midst of the assembly, I will praise you.
echoes.note: 'I will tell of your name to my brothers' is the psalmist's vow that 'I revealed your name to the people whom you gave me' (v6) enacts. Recurrence is strong (Ps 22 pervades the Johannine passion); Coherence high since the speaker declares the Name to a given community.

echoes.text: He said of his father, and of his mother, ‘I have not seen him.’ He didn’t acknowledge his brothers, nor did he know his own children; for they have observed your word, and keep your covenant.
echoes.note: 'They have kept your word' (v6) echoes Levi who 'kept your word and held to your covenant.' The covenant-fidelity idiom for the consecrated supports the priestly coloring of the prayer; low Volume, generic phrasing.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'The people whom you have given me out of the world... they were yours' (vv6,9) recasts Israel as God's own chosen possession 'out of all peoples.' Election-from-the-nations language is the coherent backdrop, though John substitutes 'world' for 'peoples'; low Volume.

echoes.text: Yes, my own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, who ate bread with me, has lifted up his heel against me.
echoes.note: 'None of them is lost except the son of destruction, that the Scripture might be fulfilled' (v12) points to 'my close friend... who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me,' the betrayal text John explicitly cites at 13:18. High Coherence and Recurrence make this the leading scriptural referent for the fulfillment formula here.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’ “So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.”
echoes.note: 'Holy Father, keep them through your name' (v11) figures the Aaronic blessing where the LORD 'keep you' and 'so shall they put my name upon the people of Israel, and I will bless them.' The conjunction of keeping + the Name placed on the people is a strong, specific structural parallel to Jesus' priestly petition.

echoes.text: and join them for you one to another into one stick, that they may become one in your hand.
echoes.note: 'That they may be one, even as we are' (v11) figures the two sticks joined 'that they may become one in your hand,' Ezekiel's sign of regathered, unified Israel. The oneness-of-the-people motif is coherent with John's unity petitions (vv21-23) and recurs there, strengthening the figural reading.

echoes.text: Let his days be few. Let another take his office.
echoes.note: 'The son of destruction' whose loss fulfills Scripture (v12) is illumined by 'may his days be few; may another take his office,' the imprecation later applied to Judas in Acts. The betrayer-who-must-be-replaced motif coheres with the fulfillment claim; medium since John does not quote it here.

echoes.text: After this, Absalom prepared him a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him. Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate. It was so, that when any man had a suit which should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called to him, and said, “What city are you from?” He said, “Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.” Absalom said to him, “Behold, your matters are good and right; but there is no man deputized by the […]
echoes.note: The 'son of destruction' (v12) is typologically prefigured by Ahithophel, David's trusted counselor who betrays him, crosses with him over the brook, and hangs himself. The David/Jesus typology with a betraying intimate provides coherent, recurrent narrative substance behind Judas; figural rather than verbal.

echoes.text: For then I will purify the lips of the peoples, that they may all call on Yahweh’s name, to serve him shoulder to shoulder.
echoes.note: Keeping the people in the Name 'that they may be one' (v11) echoes the promise that purified peoples will 'call upon the name of the LORD and serve him with one accord' (lit. one shoulder). Name + unity cluster is coherent though the Volume is faint.

echoes.text: Against whom do you sport yourselves? Against whom do you make a wide mouth, and stick out your tongue? Aren’t you children of disobedience, a seed of falsehood,
echoes.note: The Semitic idiom 'son of destruction/perdition' (v12) resembles prophetic 'children of transgression, offspring of deceit.' Supplies an OT pattern for the 'son of X' designation of the doomed, but the specific phrase is not borrowed; low Volume, contested.

harmony.title: The footwashing and farewell discourse
harmony.note: Five chapters where the Synoptics give the meal: the new commandment, the vine, the Paraclete, and the high-priestly prayer. John only.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The Lord has gone up, and we wait for the promise.
We gather in one place and pray.
With one accord the disciples kept to prayer.
We wait for the gift the Father gives.
Holy Father, keep them in your name, that they may be one.
Make us one as you are one.
Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Come up the stairs to the room where they waited, doors closed against the city, hearts turned toward a promise not yet kept.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
They were of one accord, the women and the eleven, holding to prayer in the long space between the going and the coming.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
And over them, even now, the Lord is praying: Holy Father, keep them, that they may be one as we are one.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
So we wait together, and we will not wait in vain.
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The Lord has ascended; in the upper room we wait.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
With one accord we hold to prayer.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
He prays for us: that we may be one.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
We wait for the promise. Come, let us worship.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
